subject: Request: multi-year term shelf & renewal protection for NovaMed
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: multi-year term shelf & renewal protection for NovaMed

Team —

Quick context: NovaMed (Liam O'Connor, procurement + Sara Patel, legal) is pushing for a 3-year committed purchase order and wants firm price certainty across the term. The commercial asks that require non-standard exec clearance are:

- 36-month price lock on model list pricing for the committed SKUs (no ad-hoc upstream indexation)
- Annual uplift cap of 6% (they propose 0% but not acceptable for us)
- Renewal protection: for first renewal year they want increases limited to CPI or 6%, whichever is lower, plus a clause preventing unilateral list-price jumps for 12 months post-renewal

Deal profile: 3-year commitment, expected billed ARR ~ $1.8M / year (billing cadence annual), estimated blended gross margin impact depends on quantization profile but Finance forecast attached. Procurement is insisting on these terms to pass an internal board review.

Why I recommend we approve with guardrails:
- Strategic account in healthcare with potential upsell to other lines (they're piloting our private deployment in two hospitals)
- Predictable revenue with committed minimums mitigates uplift risk

Proposed concession (recommended):
- Approve price lock & 6% uplift cap in exchange for a minimum consumption commitment: 85% of committed ARR must be consumed each 12-month period or pricing reverts to list plus a 10% surcharge on shortfall (to protect unit economics)
- Limit the discount year-1 to max 20% off list on the contracted SKUs
- Include a clause that allows Redwood to revert to compatible lower-latency/cheaper model variants if upstream cost increases materially (with 60 days' notice) — legal to scope language

Attachments: novamed-term-sheet-v2.pdf (term summary), procurement-qa.docx (their questionnaire), pricing-model-forecast.xlsx

Ask: exec clearance to proceed with counter that includes the minimum-consumption guardrail + finance sign-off and legal to include automatic rollback language. If we get a green light today/tomorrow I can push a signed PO and get procurement to start onboarding.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior AE, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-year term shelf & renewal protection for NovaMed

Aditya —

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. A couple of clarifying questions before I route to Legal/Finance for final language: 

1) The 85% consumption threshold — is that % based on booked usage (tokens/compute) or billed ARR? We should pick one and be explicit in the term sheet.
2) If we include the 10% surcharge on shortfall, do we still want a shortfall cure period (30 days) to allow the account to demonstrate usage?
3) Please confirm blended margin impact in the attachment if we accept 6% uplift cap vs. indexation — I asked Finance to highlight delta for FY1-FY3 but haven't seen final commentary.

If answers are straightforward and Finance signs off on the model, I don't have sensitivity to approving the 6% cap with the consumption guardrail. I want Legal to hard-stop on the automatic rollback language — it needs precise trigger and notice windows.

-Marissa
VP, Deal Desk

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>, Contracts <contracts@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-year term shelf & renewal protection for NovaMed

Marissa —

Answers inline:
1) Consumption basis: propose we tie 85% to billed ARR (committed consumption as invoiced) rather than raw token usage. Procurement wants usage-based protection, but billing tie simplifies enforcement and auditability. If Legal prefers usage metrics we can add an audit right.
2) Shortfall cure: yes — propose 30-day cure to avoid accidental reversion for minor timing differences.
3) Finance note: attached pricing-model-forecast.xlsx has a tab "rev-impact" — short summary: approving 6% uplift cap vs indexation reduces expected gross margin by ~2.4 percentage points over three years at current usage mix; mitigated by the 85% consumption guardrail which recovers ~60% of that delta in the model. Ben, please confirm if that matches your numbers.

Fallback if exec wants less exposure:
- We can offer a 24-month instead of 36-month price lock with same uplift cap; or
- Keep 36 months but lower the uplift cap to 4% if Finance insists — but that will increase discount pressure on initial pricing.

If I don't hear objections by EOD tomorrow, I'll ask Legal to draft the clause language and share the updated term sheet for signatures.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-year term shelf & renewal protection for NovaMed

Appreciated the clear framing and options. I'm granting conditional executive clearance to proceed with the following constraints: 

1) Approve 36-month price lock with 6% annual uplift cap, conditional on:
   - Minimum billed ARR consumption of 85% per 12-month period, measured against the committed ARR on the signed PO.
   - 30-day cure period for shortfalls.
   - If consumption falls below 60% in any 12-month period, Redwood may exercise the rollback clause immediately and reprice to list + 10% surcharge for the remainder of the term.
2) Maximum year-1 discount off list: 20% (no exceptions).
3) Legal must insert precise rollback triggers, auditability language, and a 60-day notice window for any model-variant switch; DocuSign route to be used for signatures.
4) Finance (Ben) to confirm the final pricing-model forecast and sign off prior to countersigning.

Marissa/Ben: please confirm you can operationalize the consumption measurement and finance checks. Aditya: proceed to get Legal to draft the term with these guardrails and share the updated term sheet back to the thread. Once Legal and Finance sign off, I authorize Sales to accept PO and proceed to onboarding.

Kimberly Park
VP, Sales (Americas)
Redwood Inference

--
Thread notes: Legal to draft clause; aditya to return final term sheet; expected next items: DocuSign routing and finance sign-off.
